question: Identify the set in which all species are isoelectronic.
explanation: All sets listed contain species with identical electron counts (18, 10, and 10 electrons respectively).

question: Which ion has the smallest radius among O<sup>2-</sup>, F<sup>-</sup>, Na<sup>+</sup>, and Mg<sup>2+</sup>?
explanation: Mg<sup>2+</sup> has the highest nuclear charge (Z = 12) for 10 electrons, creating the greatest inward pull.

Which of the following is isoelectronic with carbon monoxide (CO)?
explanation: CO, CN<sup>-</sup>, N<sub>2</sub>, and NO<sup>+</sup> all possess 14 electrons.

question: How does ionic radius vary across an isoelectronic series as atomic number increases?
explanation: As atomic number increases, nuclear charge increases while electron count remains constant, causing ionic radius to decrease.

question: Which of the following pairs has the same number of electrons?
explanation: K<sup>+</sup> has 18 electrons and Cl<sup>-</sup> has 18 electrons.

question: Which of the following species has 10 electrons and a nuclear charge of +9?
explanation: Nuclear charge +9 corresponds to fluorine (Z = 9), and with 10 electrons it is the fluoride ion F<sup>-</sup>.

question: In the isoelectronic series P<sup>3-</sup>, S<sup>2-</sup>, and Cl<sup>-</sup>, which has the highest ionization energy?
explanation: Cl<sup>-</sup> has the highest nuclear charge (Z = 17) among them, holding its electrons most tightly and requiring the highest energy to remove.

question: Which molecule is isoelectronic with BF<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup>?
explanation: BF<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> has 5 + 4(9) + 1 = 42 electrons. CF<sub>4</sub> has 6 + 36 = 42 electrons. NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> has 10 + 32 = 42 electrons? Wait: N(7)+4(1)-1 = 10, F has 9 each so 4F = 36, 10+36=46. Ah, BF<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> is isoelectronic with CF<sub>4</sub> (both have 42 valence electrons total). Let's verify: B(3) + 4(7) + 1 = 32 valence electrons. C(4) + 4(7) = 32 valence electrons. Thus BF<sub>4</sub><sup>-</sup> and CF<sub>4</sub> are valence-isoelectronic.

question: Which property is expected to be identical for two isoelectronic neutral molecules?
explanation: By definition, isoelectronic species share an identical total number of electrons.
